identities.label: Mattaponi
identities.summary:
The Mattaponi (English:  ) tribe is one of only two Virginia Indian tribes in the Commonwealth of Virginia that owns reservation land, which it has held since the colonial era.  The larger Mattaponi Indian Tribe lives in King William County on the reservation, which stretches along the borders of the Mattaponi River, near West Point, Virginia.
The Mattaponi were one of six tribes inherited by the leader of the Confederacy, Mamanatowick Powhatan, in the late 16th century.  The tribe spoke an Algonquian language, like other members of the Powhatan Confederacy.
